original_value: Urban traffic light control is an important and challenging real-world problem. By regarding intersections as agents, most of the Reinforcement Learning (RL) based methods generate actions of agents independently. They can cause action conflict and result in overflow or road resource waste in adjacent intersections. Recently, some collaborative methods have alleviated the above problems by extending the observable surroundings of agents, which can be considered as inactive cross-agent communication methods. However, when agents act synchronously in these works, the perceived action value is biased and the information exchanged is insufficient. In this work, we propose a novel Multi-agent Communication and Action Rectification (MaCAR) framework. It enables active communication between agents by considering the impact of synchronous actions of agents. MaCAR consists of two parts: (1) an active Communication Agent Network (CAN) involving a Message Propagation Graph Neural Network (MPGNN); (2) a Traffic Forecasting Network (TFN) which learns to predict the traffic after agents' synchronous actions and the corresponding action values. By using predicted information, we mitigate the action value bias during training to help rectify agents' future actions. In experiments, we show that our proposal can outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

result.paraphrase: Urban traffic signal control is a difficult and important real-world challenge. Treating intersections as agents, most reinforcement-learning-based methods choose each agent’s actions independently, which can lead to action conflicts and cause overflow or wasted road capacity at neighboring intersections. More recently, collaborative approaches have reduced these issues by enlarging each agent’s observable area, effectively serving as inactive cross-agent communication. Yet when agents act simultaneously in these methods, the perceived action values become biased and the exchanged information remains limited. To address this, we propose a new Multi-agent Communication and Action Rectification (MaCAR) framework that supports active communication among agents by accounting for the effects of synchronized actions. MaCAR has two components: (1) an active Communication Agent Network (CAN) that includes a Message Propagation Graph Neural Network (MPGNN); and (2) a Traffic Forecasting Network (TFN) that learns to predict post-synchronization traffic and the associated action values. Using the predicted information, we reduce action-value bias during training to help correct agents’ future actions. Experiments show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
